title: Kotlin
description: Language features, null safety, generics, coroutines and Flow.

questions.question: Which functions does a data class generate automatically?
questions.explanation: Only properties in the primary constructor are used by the generated functions.

questions.question: Which scope function uses 'this' as receiver and returns the receiver object?
questions.explanation: apply: this → receiver. also: it → receiver. let: it → lambda result. run: this → lambda result.

questions.question: Where can 'const val' be used?

answers.text: Top level or in an object/companion object, with primitive or String values
For any val inside a class

questions.explanation: const values are compile-time constants and are inlined at the call site.

questions.question: Which statements about lateinit are correct?

answers.text: Not allowed for primitive types like Int
Accessing it before initialization throws UninitializedPropertyAccessException

questions.explanation: Use ::prop.isInitialized to check. For primitives, use Delegates.notNull() instead.

questions.question: What is the default thread-safety mode of 'by lazy { }'?
questions.explanation: Use lazy(LazyThreadSafetyMode.NONE) when you know only one thread accesses it, e.g. UI code.

questions.question: What makes 'when' over a sealed class useful?

answers.text: The compiler checks that all subclasses are handled when used as an expression
Sealed classes can be extended by any module

questions.explanation: Subclasses of a sealed class must be in the same module and package, so the set is known at compile time.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and === in Kotlin?

answers.text: == checks structural equality (equals); === checks reference identity

questions.explanation: a == b is translated to a?.equals(b) ?: (b === null).

questions.question: How are extension functions dispatched?

answers.text: Statically, based on the declared type of the receiver
Virtually, based on the runtime type

questions.explanation: Extensions don't modify classes. A member function with the same signature always wins.

questions.question: What does 'out' in 'interface Source<out T>' mean?

answers.text: T is covariant: Source<String> is a subtype of Source<Any>
T can only be used as a parameter type

questions.explanation: out = producer (T only returned). in = consumer (T only accepted), e.g. Comparator<in T>.

questions.question: Why is 'reified' only allowed in inline functions?

answers.text: The type argument is substituted at the call site, so it's available at runtime
Reified types are stored in the class file metadata
It's a JVM limitation for lambdas

questions.explanation: Normally generics are erased; inlining copies the body with the concrete type, e.g. for 'is T' checks.

questions.question: What is the difference between launch and async?

answers.text: launch returns a Job; async returns a Deferred with a result
async uncaught exceptions are thrown on await()

questions.explanation: Both start a coroutine in the given scope; neither blocks.

questions.question: Which dispatcher is meant for blocking I/O such as file or network access?
questions.explanation: Default is for CPU-heavy work (threads = CPU cores); IO allows many more threads for blocking calls.

questions.question: What does withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { ... } do?

answers.text: Runs the block on the IO dispatcher, suspends the caller and returns the block's result
Starts a new coroutine and returns immediately
Blocks the main thread until done

questions.explanation: It's the standard way to make a suspending function main-safe.

questions.question: Which statements about StateFlow are correct?

answers.text: It always has a value and needs an initial value
New collectors immediately get the current value
Equal consecutive values are not emitted again (conflation/distinctUntilChanged)

questions.explanation: StateFlow is a hot flow. For events without state, use SharedFlow or Channel.

questions.question: A regular flow { ... } builder creates…

answers.text: a cold flow: the code runs anew for each collector
a hot flow shared by all collectors

questions.explanation: Use shareIn/stateIn to turn a cold flow into a hot one.

questions.question: What does SupervisorJob change?

answers.text: A failing child doesn't cancel its siblings or the parent
Children can't be cancelled at all

questions.explanation: viewModelScope and lifecycleScope use a SupervisorJob.

questions.question: Why should you not swallow CancellationException in a catch-all block in a coroutine?

answers.text: It breaks cooperative cancellation: the coroutine keeps running although it was cancelled
It isn't possible to catch it

questions.explanation: Rethrow CancellationException or use ensureActive() / catch more specific exceptions.

questions.question: What does @JvmOverloads do?

answers.text: Generates Java overloads for functions with default parameters

questions.explanation: Useful for custom Views: constructors with (Context), (Context, AttributeSet), …

questions.question: What is a value class (@JvmInline value class)?

answers.text: A wrapper around one value that is usually represented by the underlying value at runtime
A class that can only hold primitive values

questions.explanation: Gives type safety (e.g. UserId vs. String) mostly without allocation overhead.

questions.question: Does Kotlin have checked exceptions?
questions.explanation: Use @Throws when Java callers need to know about exceptions.
